grades.reason: Covers fork/exec behavior and process IDs. It says nothing about pipes, EOF, or file descriptor closing, so it doesn't help diagnose the missing EOF.

grades.quote: The pipe code sleeps inside a loop checking the sleep condition; if there are multiple readers or writers, all but the first process to wake up will see the condition is false and sleep again.
grades.reason: Describes how xv6 piperead and pipewrite block and wake with sleep/wakeup, so it gives background on why a reader blocks. It never discusses EOF or the write end being closed, which is the likely cause of the problem.

grades.quote: If no data is available, a read on a pipe waits for either data to be written or for all file descriptors referring to the write end to be closed; in the latter case, read will return 0, just as if the end of a data file had been reached. The fact that read blocks until it is impossible for new data to arrive is one reason that it’s important for the child to close the write end of the pipe before executing wc above: if one of wc ’s file descriptors referred to the write end of the pipe, wc would never see end-of-file.
grades.reason: Directly explains the cause. A pipe read returns EOF (0) only after every file descriptor for the write end is closed. If any process still holds the write end open, such as the parent or a child that didn't close it, the reader blocks and never sees EOF. It also shows the fix of closing the unused ends.
Covers waitpid, zombies, and reaping child processes. It has no connection to pipe file descriptors or EOF, and a zombie's existence doesn't explain a missing EOF.
